\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Probability of an answer]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ansProb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ansProb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.narun, Randomized.randProb}
For a nondeterministic register program $A$, an oracle, an input $x$, an initial
configuration $a$, a natural number $N$, and an answer bit $b$, define the probability
of answer $b$ to be the probability, over the length-$N$ random choice string, that the
resulting run returns $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probability semantics for a program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NTerm, Complexity.LogProg.ansProb}
For a nondeterministic register program $A$, an oracle, an input $x$, a guard $G$ on
configurations, an initial configuration $a$, and a rational number $p$, define
probability semantics to mean that $A$ terminates from $a$ under guard $G$ and that, for
every natural number $N$ for which all length-$N$ choice strings halt from $a$, the
probability of returning true is $p$ and the probability of returning false is $1-p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Congruence of probabilistic semantics]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.PSem}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a randomized program with finitely many registers and deciders, let $O$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be an input, let $G$ be a predicate on configurations, and let $a$ be an
initial configuration. If the program has probabilistic semantics with parameter
$p\in\mathbb{Q}$ from $a$ under $G$, and $p=q$, then it has probabilistic semantics with
parameter $q$ from the same configuration under the same guard. Here probabilistic
semantics means that every sequence of choices leads to termination while respecting
$G$, and, for every number $N$ of random bits for which all length-$N$ choice sequences
halt and satisfy the guard at each earlier live step, the probabilities of returning
true and false are respectively $q$ and $1-q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Semantics of a Halted Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.halted}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.halted}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.ansProb, Complexity.LogProg.narun_halted, Randomized.randProb_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle and input, and let $v$ be any
register assignment. A halted configuration with answer
$b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ has probabilistic semantics with probability $1$
if $b$ is true and $0$ if $b$ is false, for any guard $G$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Complexity.LogProg.succ_of_nhalts}

\begin{lemma}[Acceptance probability after a fair choice]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.choose}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.choose}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.of_choose, Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.ansProb, Complexity.LogProg.nastep, Complexity.LogProg.nastep_choose, Complexity.LogProg.randProb_narun_choose, Complexity.LogProg.succ_of_nhalts}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a machine with $m$ natural-number registers, control labels in $$, and
instructions that may choose between two labels using a fair random bit; let $$ be an
oracle, $x$ an input, and $G$ a guard on configurations. Suppose the instruction at
label $l$ chooses between $l_1$ and $l_0$, and the configuration with label $l$,
register values $v$, and no result satisfies $G$. If starting at $l_1$ with register
values $v$ and no result terminates under $G$ with acceptance probability $p_1$, and
starting at $l_0$ under the same conditions terminates under $G$ with acceptance
probability $p_0$, then starting at $l$ terminates under $G$ with acceptance probability
$(p_1+p_0)/2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Preservation under clearing a register]

register $r$ and moves to state $l'$, and suppose $G$ holds at $(l,v,	ext{none})$. If

\begin{lemma}[Preservation of semantics under a positive oracle call]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos}

Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle
deciders, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $G$ be a guard on configurations. Suppose the

with the single argument register $r$ and destinations $l_1$ and $l_0$. If $G$ holds at
the configuration with label $l$, register contents $v$, and no answer yet, and the

\begin{theorem}[Copying a register in a probabilistic program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.psem_copy}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.psem_copy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ natural-number registers, state
set $\Lambda$, and oracle, and fix an input $x$ and register bound $B$. Let $dst$ and
$src$ be distinct register indices. Suppose state $test$ compares them, going to $ex$ if
they are equal and to $bump$ otherwise, and state $bump$ increments $dst$ and returns to
$test$. For any rational $p$ and register valuation $v$ bounded by $B$ with $v(dst)\le
v(src)$, if the configuration at $ex$ with $dst$ set to $v(src)$ has probabilistic
semantics of acceptance probability $p$, then the configuration at $test$ with valuation
$v$ has the same semantics and acceptance probability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two additions in a probabilistic program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.psem_addTwice}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.psem_addTwice}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{7}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ natural-number registers, state
set $\Lambda$, and oracle, and fix an input $x$ and register bound $B$. Let $k,y,p$ be
register indices with $k\ne y$, $k\ne p$, and $p\ne y$. Suppose the instruction at
$test$ compares registers $k$ and $y$, going to $ex$ when they are equal and to $i_1$
otherwise; $i_1,i_2,i_3$ successively increment register $p$, with $i_3$ also
incrementing $k$ and returning to $test$. For any rational $q$ and register valuation
$v$ bounded by $B$, assume $v(k)\le v(y)$ and $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))\le B$. If, for the
configuration at $ex$ with register $p$ increased by $2(v(y)-v(k))$ and register $k$ set
to $v(y)$, the probabilistic semantics has acceptance probability $q$, then the
configuration at $test$ with valuation $v$ has the same semantics and acceptance
probability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probabilistic semantics from deterministic reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.of_areach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.of_areach}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart_choose, Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.det, Complexity.LogProg.arun, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases, Complexity.LogProg.nastep_det, Complexity.LogProg.nastep_det'}

register valuation $v'$, and rational $p$ be given. Suppose the configuration
$(l',v',	ext{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$.
Then, for every natural number $T$ and configuration $a$, if running the program with
each choice resolved as false for $T$ steps takes $a$ to $(l',v',	ext{no answer})$, and
the guard holds at every configuration along that run before time $T$, the initial
configuration $a$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Ascending search reaches the first positive test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.searchUp_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.searchUp_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let a register machine have $m$ registers, states in a type $\Lambda$, and an oracle on
$d$ Boolean-string inputs. Fix a register $r$, a decidable predicate $P$ on the natural
numbers, states $\mathrm{test},\mathrm{inc},\mathrm{yes}\in\Lambda$, a bound $B$, and a
register valuation $v$ with every register at most $B$. Assume that from state
$\mathrm{test}$, with register $r$ set to any $c'$, one step leaves the registers
unchanged and goes to $\mathrm{yes}$ if $P(c')$ holds and to $\mathrm{inc}$ otherwise;
also assume every configuration at state $\mathrm{test}$ with no result satisfies the
machine's precondition, and that state $\mathrm{inc}$ increments register $r$ and
returns to $\mathrm{test}$. Let $c$ satisfy $P(c)$ and $c\le B$. For every $c_0\le c$
such that no $c'$ with $c_0\le c'<c$ satisfies $P(c')$, the machine can reach the
configuration at state $\mathrm{yes}$ with register valuation $v$ updated to $c$ at $r$
and no result, starting from state $\mathrm{test}$ with that register set to $c_0$ and
no result; throughout this run, every visited configuration before the final one
satisfies the guard requiring the precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Descending search reaches the first positive test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.searchDown_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.searchDown_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let a register machine have $m$ registers, states in a type $\Lambda$, and an oracle on
$d$ Boolean-string inputs. Fix a register $r$, a decidable predicate $P$ on the natural
numbers, states $\mathrm{test},\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{dec}\in\Lambda$, a bound $B$, and a
register valuation $v$ with every register at most $B$. Assume that from state
$\mathrm{test}$, with register $r$ set to any $c'$, one step leaves the registers
unchanged and goes to $\mathrm{yes}$ if $P(c')$ holds and to $\mathrm{dec}$ otherwise;
also assume every configuration at state $\mathrm{test}$ with no result satisfies the
machine's precondition, and that state $\mathrm{dec}$ decrements register $r$ and
returns to $\mathrm{test}$. For any $c$ satisfying $P(c)$, every $c_0$ with $c<c_0\le B$
and with no $c'$ strictly between $c$ and $c_0$ satisfying $P(c')$, the machine can
reach the configuration at state $\mathrm{yes}$ with register valuation $v$ updated to
$c$ at $r$ and no result, starting from state $\mathrm{dec}$ with that register set to
$c_0$ and no result; throughout this run, every visited configuration before the final
one satisfies the guard requiring the precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

deciders, let $x$ be a bit string, let $G$ be a predicate on configurations, and let $p$
be a rational number. Suppose that at a control state $l$, the machine executes a call
to decider $j$ with mode $md$ and register list $args$, branching to $l_1$ on a positive
answer and to $l_0$ on a negative answer. For a register valuation $v$, suppose $G$
holds of the configuration at $l$ with valuation $v$ and no answer yet, and that the
configuration reached by this call—at $l_1$ or $l_0$ according to the oracle's answer on
the virtual input formed from $x$ and the binary words of the listed registers—has
probabilistic semantics $p$ under $G$. Then the configuration at $l$ with valuation $v$
and no answer yet also has probabilistic semantics $p$ under $G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Semantics of a Decrement Step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.dec}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.dec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.det, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input, guard $G$, and
probability $p$. Suppose its instruction at control state $l$ is the deterministic
instruction that replaces register $r$ by $\max(v(r)-1,0)$ and moves to $l'$. If the
current configuration satisfies $G$ and the resulting configuration has probabilistic
semantics with probability $p$, then the current configuration also has probabilistic
semantics with probability $p$.
\end{lemma}
